whats_new.title: PSL from the camera
items: The camera now suggests Pakistan Sign Language words. It learned them from a public PSL dataset of hand movements (SignSpeak).
Every PSL answer is a suggestion (Tier B) that you confirm. Nothing is spoken until you tap "Yes".
These signs are marked "Community dataset — not yet validated" until Deaf signers check them.
Your confirmations tune the suggestions to your own signing. This is kept only in your browser, and "Forget them" removes it.
A five-second camera check tells you if the light, distance or framing will cause problems.

whats_new.title: Talking both ways
items: Confirmed signs build a sentence in English or Urdu, with the signs you made shown underneath.
The hearing person can type a reply. It is shown in large text, and the words SignBridge knows play as PSL dictionary videos, word by word.
Quick phrases and emergency phrases speak with one tap.

whats_new.title: Seeing how signs are made
items: The dictionary videos are back for 31 vocabulary words.
A new Dictionary page lists every sign of a community PSL dictionary, each with its video.

whats_new.title: ASL mode
items: ASL mode runs in the background again. On the old site its model could not load in a Web Worker and ran on the main page instead.
It speaks a word only when it is at least 70 % sure.

whats_new.title: Faster, offline and clearer
items: The first visit loads less: the camera software and ASL mode load only when you use them.
"Save for offline use" stores the whole site on your device, so it works with no internet.
Text is larger and easier to read everywhere.
New pages: "How well it works" (every measured number, with where and how it was measured), "Credits and licences" and this page.

whats_new.title: Still limited
items: No sign is Tier A ("Recognised") yet. That needs a test on people the model has never seen, and a Deaf validator's sign-off.
Finger-spelling is not included: there is no licensed PSL letter data the app could learn from yet.
The PSL camera knows 70+ words, not full sentences signed without pauses.
